title: fmpz exact word and container closure
objective: Complete the next fail-closed resident-fmpz slice by supporting exact NativeIntegerVector indices, checked fmpz-to-uint64 conversion, borrowed UInt64Buffer operations with Python indexing semantics, and exact integer modulo uint64 without mpz bridges, with differential and sanitizer evidence

oracles: dynamic JavaScript, GMP, tagged, word, and fmpz differential execution
generated fmpz internal code contains no mpz conversion or host callback

handoff.summary: Adds allocation-free direct-fmpz checked uint64 conversion and floor modulo, exact NativeIntegerVector indices with pre-mutation validation, and borrowed UInt64Buffer get/set/length with Python negative indexing. Generated internal fmpz functions remain free of mpz bridges and host callbacks. Focused differential tests cover fmpz/GMP/tagged/JavaScript plus ordinary CPython, immutable input leases, aliasing, promoted and 4096-bit values, boundary failures with unchanged outputs, and ASan/UBSan checks of direct vector helpers. The obsolete checked-uint64 fail-closed witnesses now use exact range, which remains deliberately unsupported for the next serialized lane.
risks: The portable modulus helper is compiled and directly checked on a 64-bit FLINT host for moduli above 32-bit range, but actual FLINT_BITS=32 execution depends on downstream cross-platform CI.

pnpm test:changed passed its full build plus native-architecture and WebAssembly audit subchecks, then stopped because the merge-owned optimizer-opportunity artifact manifest is stale after compiler changes; it did not reach the remaining unit/native/Wasm test umbrellas, and this lane does not claim or regenerate that shared artifact.
next_steps: The exact-range/ownership lane should use this word/container support to remove the remaining borrowed-vector GMP ownership blocker in the 83-function cubic closure.
Integration should regenerate the optimizer-opportunity artifacts, rerun the mandatory full architecture/native validation, and exercise Linux arm64, macOS arm64, and Windows x64 CI.
